blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Agentic AI extends large language models (LLMs) from generating responses to planning and executing complex workflows, substantially expanding their utility while exposing applications to unsafe actions, information leakage, and adversarial manipulation. Multi-agent systems further expand these capabilities through specialization and collaboration, but distributed authority, heterogeneous roles, and opaque or potentially compromised participants make safeguarding even more challenging. Existing defenses address important individual threats but provide fragmented coverage across local execution, system-level interactions, and enforcement mechanisms. We introduce MAS-Guard, a unified framework that closes this gap for safeguarding single- and multi-agent AI applications containing both instrumentable and opaque agents. Within instrumentable agents, the proposed local Agent Guardrail (A-Guard) layer applies task-specific experts to assess agentic events. At the system level, developer-owned Agent Charters and a Control Plane combine deterministic structural checks of routes, agent capabilities, and message formats with semantic assessments of roles and message content. These complementary layers enable enforcement through a shared set of interventions: allow, reflection, confirmation, and block. Evaluated across six benchmarks covering diverse single- and multi-agent scenarios with three agent LLMs from different providers, MAS-Guard reduces the overall attack success rate by 71.5-86.3% relative to unguarded agents, while meeting the utility reference criterion on benign tasks.
blocks.zh: Agentic AI扩展了大型语言模型(LLMs),从生成对复杂工作流程的规划和实施的响应,大幅扩展其效用,同时将应用程序暴露于不安全的行动,信息泄露,以及对抗性操纵. 多代理系统通过专业化和协作进一步扩大了这些能力,但分布式权威、不同的作用以及不透明或可能受到损害的参与者使保障更加困难。 现有辩护处理重要的个别威胁,但涉及地方执行、系统层面互动和执行机制。 我们引入了MAS-Guard,这个统一的框架可以弥补保护单剂和多剂AI应用的这一缺口,这些应用既包括仪器,也包括不透明的剂. 在有仪器的代理中,拟议的当地代理Guardrail(A-Guard)层应用特定任务的专家来评估代理事件。 在系统一级,开发商拥有的代理合同和控制计划将确定路线、代理能力和信息格式的结构检查与对角色和信息内容的语义评估结合起来。 这些相辅相成的层面通过一套共同的干预措施得以执行:允许、反思、确认和阻断。 MAS-Guard对涵盖不同单一和多代理情景的6个基准进行了评估,其中包含来自不同供应商的3个代理LLMs,将整体攻击成功率相对于无人看守的代理降低了71.5%-86.3%,同时达到了良性任务的效用参考标准。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Figure 1: MAS-Guard combines system-level safeguards defined by Agent Charters and Control Plane configuration with agent-local A-Guard checks to protect interactions among users, agents, and tools.
blocks.zh: 图1:MAS-Guard将代理宪章和控制计划配置界定的系统级保障措施与代理-当地A-Guard检查相结合,以保护用户、代理人和工具之间的互动。

blocks.en: Large language model (LLM) agents extend text generation into action by retrieving data, invoking tools, and collaborating with other agents. Tool-selection errors or malicious instructions in retrieved content can trigger irreversible actions or disclose sensitive information. Recent studies report vulnerabilities such as indirect prompt injection through tool outputs, taking unsafe actions, and observation or memory poisoning ( Ruan et al., 2024 ; Greshake et al., 2023 ; Zhan et al., 2024 ; Debenedetti et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) .
blocks.zh: 大型语言模型(LLM)代理通过检索数据,引用工具,与其他代理合作,将文本生成扩展为动作. 工具选择错误或检索内容中的恶意指令可触发不可逆转的行动或披露敏感信息. 近期的研究表明存在脆弱性,如通过工具输出间接迅速注射,采取不安全行动,以及观察或记忆中毒(Ruan等人,2024年;Greshake等人,2023年;Zhan等人,2024年;Debenedetti等人,2024年;Zhang等人,2025年)。

blocks.en: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built from LLM agents expand this attack surface. Inter-agent messages serve simultaneously as task data and control signals; consequently, a local failure can propagate through delegation, shared context, and downstream tool access. Attacks can spread injected instructions across agents, manipulate communication channels, or disclose sensitive information ( Lee and Tiwari, 2024 ; He et al., 2025 ; Patil et al., 2025 ; An et al., 2026 ; Kavathekar et al., 2026 ; El Yagoubi et al., 2026 ; Naik et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 由LLM剂制造的多剂系统(MAS)扩展了这个攻击表面. 代理信息同时作为任务数据和控制信号;因此,局部失败可以通过授权、共享上下文和下游工具访问传播。 攻击可以跨越毒剂注入指令,操纵通信渠道,或披露敏感信息(Lee和Tiwari,2024年;He等人,2025年;Patil等人,2025年;An等人,2026年;Kavathekar等人,2026年;El Yagoubi等人,2026年;Naik等人,2026年)。

blocks.en:
Furthermore, real-world deployments may combine instrumentable agents , whose runtime allow guardrails to inspect and stop tool calls or messages, with opaque agents , such as third-party services that expose only a request–response interface.
AI safety risks are especially difficult to govern when a deployment combines instrumentable agents, whose execution loops support local guardrail integration, with opaque agents, accessible only through their external interfaces: no individual agent observes the full context, yet unsafe behavior can emerge at the shared boundaries.
blocks.zh:
此外,现实世界的部署可能将可装仪器的代理(其运行时间允许看守员检查和停止工具呼叫或消息)与不透明的代理(例如仅披露请求-响应接口的第三方服务)结合起来。
AI安全风险在部署时结合了可仪器剂,其执行循环支持本地的护栏整合,与不透明剂,只能通过外部接口进入:没有单个代理人观察整个背景,然而在共享边界上会出现不安全的行为.

blocks.en: Existing defenses provide pieces of the solution. Prompt-isolation and injection-detection methods protect untrusted context; trajectory guard models audit agent behavior; tool-call guards intervene before execution; and policy or information-flow systems enforce structured restrictions ( Hines et al., 2024 ; Chennabasappa et al., 2025 ; Mou et al., 2026 ; Liu et al., 2026b ; Costa et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) . However, the literature remains fragmented along three dimensions. Surface fragmentation yields defenses specialized for prompt injection, tool use, or another isolated failure mode. Scope fragmentation leaves most safeguards centered on one agent rather than the routes, roles, and trust boundaries of the composed application. Enforcement fragmentation makes it difficult to apply a consistent intervention policy across heterogeneous guardrails. Multi-agent defenses based on anomaly detection or permitted control-flow graphs address important subsets of these problems ( Zhou et al., 2025 ; Jha et al., 2026 ) , but do not by themselves provide a common guardrail layer spanning local agent execution and cross-agent boundaries.
blocks.zh: 现有的防御提供了解决方案的片段. 快速隔离和注射检测方法保护不信任的背景;轨迹守卫模式审计代理行为;工具呼叫守卫在执行前进行干预;政策或信息流系统执行结构化限制(Hines等人,2024年;Chennabasappa等人,2025年;Mou等人,2026年;Liu等人,2026年b;Costa等人,2025年;Wang等人,2026年)。 然而,这些文献在三个方面仍然支离破碎。 表面破碎产生专门用于迅速注射、工具使用或其他孤立故障模式的防御。 范围分散使得大多数保障措施都集中在一种物剂上,而不是放在所组成的应用的路线、作用和信任界限上。 由于执法不成体系,很难在各种护栏之间适用一致的干预政策。 基于异常探测或允许的控制流图的多剂防御解决了这些问题中的重要子集(周等人,2025年;Jha等人,2026年),但本身并不能提供跨越当地代理执行和跨代理边界的共同护栏层.

blocks.en:
We introduce Multi-Agent System Guardrail, MAS-Guard , a unified runtime guardrail framework for applications containing one or more LLM agents. MAS-Guard operates over observable events at user–agent, agent–tool, and agent–agent boundaries (Figure 1 ).
Here, a single-agent deployment is the special case with one agent and no agent–agent edges.
For instrumentable agents, a local Agent Guardrail (A-Guard) layer selects task-specific experts for agentic events such as user inputs, tool calls, tool results, and final responses (Figure 2 ). At the system level, lightweight, developer-specified Agent Charters specify each agent’s intended role, input/output boundaries, and capabilities, while a Control Plane registers agents, governs communication routes, and configures deterministic and semantic safeguards.
In MAS-Guard, all safeguards share a common intervention space— allow , reflect , confirm , and block , facilitating balanced choices between maintaining the user experience and enforcing agentic safety.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了多代理系统护卫,MAS护卫,一个用于包含一个或多个LLM剂的应用程序的统一运行时间护卫框架. MAS-Guard在用户-代理、代理-工具、代理-代理边界运行可观察到的事件(图1)。
这里,单代理部署是特例,只有一个代理,没有代理-代理边缘.
对于可仪器代理,一个本地代理Guardrail(A-Guard)层为代理事件,如用户输入,工具呼叫,工具结果,以及最终响应,选择任务特定专家(图2). 在系统一级,轻量级、开发商指定的代理人宪章规定了每个代理人的预期作用、输入/输出界限和能力,而控制计划则对代理人进行登记,管理通信路线,并配置确定性和语义性保障。
在MAS-Guard中,所有保障措施都有一个共同的干预空间——允许、反映、确认和封锁,促进在保持用户经验和加强代理安全之间作出平衡的选择。

blocks.en: Our contributions are as follows: • We introduce the Agent Guardrail (A-Guard), an extensible local defense layer for instrumentable agents. A-Guard selects event-specific experts, evaluates them, and exposes a shared verdict interface for intervention before content delivery or tool execution. • We propose a unified framework for applications combining instrumentable and opaque agents under a trusted and instrumentable MAS orchestration layer. We devise developer-owned Agent Charters and a Control Plane that connect local safeguards to system-level policy through deterministic structural checks, semantic compliance assessments, and consistent enforcement options. • To assess whether the framework’s benefits extend across agent models from different providers, we evaluate GPT-5.6-Terra OpenAI (2026c) , Muse-Glimmer-30B Meta (2026) , and Grok-4.3 SpaceXAI (2026) on six benchmarks, against eight defense methods and the unguarded baseline. The evaluation spans various prompt injection attack patterns, compromised multi-agent collaboration, privacy leakage, reasoning slowdown, and unsafe tool execution. MAS-Guard reduces the overall attack success rate by 71.5–86.3% while retaining benign task utility for each agent.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Early work examines unsafe actions for under-specified requests through ToolEmu ( Ruan et al., 2024 ) and indirect prompt injection through retrieved content ( Greshake et al., 2023 ) . InjecAgent, AgentDojo, and Agent Security Bench evaluate injection and related failures in individual-agent environments ( Zhan et al., 2024 ; Debenedetti et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ) , motivating safeguards at local execution boundaries.
blocks.zh: 早期工作通过TolleEmu(Ruan等人,2024年)和通过检索内容间接即时注射(Greshake等人,2023年),对规格不足的请求进行不安全行动审查。 InjecAgent, Agent Dojo, Associate Security Bench)评价个人代理环境中的注射及相关故障(Zhan等人,2024年;Debenedetti等人,2024年;张等人,2025年),激励当地执行边界的保障措施.

blocks.en: Runtime defenses intervene at different stages. Sandwich reinforces task instructions ( Schulhoff, 2024 ) , while Delimiter marks untrusted content ( Hines et al., 2024 ) . ACI-Sentinel filters outputs for query relevance ( An et al., 2026 ) . LlamaFirewall combines prompt-injection, alignment, and code-safety checks ( Chennabasappa et al., 2025 ) ; ToolSafe assesses tool invocations and provides corrective feedback ( Mou et al., 2026 ) ; and AgentDoG audits agent trajectories ( Liu et al., 2026b ; Liu et al., 2026a ) . FIDES alters access pattern to untrusted content using sandboxed access and query mechanisms ( Costa et al., 2025 ) , and AgentSpec applies trigger–predicate–enforcement rules ( Wang et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 运行时防守在不同阶段进行干预. 桑威奇强化了任务指令(Schulhoff, 2024 ),而Delimiter则标注了不信任的内容(Hines等人, 2024 ). ACI-Sentinel 为查询关联性过滤输出(An等人,2026年) . Llama Firewall将快速注射、调整和密码安全检查结合起来(Chennabasappa等人,2025年);TolleSafe评估工具引用和提供纠正反馈(Mou等人,2026年);Agent DoG审计代理轨迹(Liu等人,2026年b;Liu等人,2026年a)。 FIDES使用沙箱式访问和查询机制将访问模式改变为不信任的内容(Costa等人,2025年),AgentSpec适用触发(preptect)-执行规则(Wang等人,2026年)。

blocks.en: Multi-agent systems introduce additional risks. Prompt Infection and Agent-in-the-Middle attacks exploit instruction propagation and inter-agent communication ( Lee and Tiwari, 2024 ; He et al., 2025 ) . Privacy studies expose information leakage and exfiltration ( Patil et al., 2025 ; El Yagoubi et al., 2026 ; Naik et al., 2026 ) , while TAMAS and ACIArena study attacks across frameworks and topologies ( Kavathekar et al., 2026 ; An et al., 2026 ) . Defenses include GUARDIAN’s error propagation model ( Zhou et al., 2025 ) and ControlValve’s control-flow constraints ( Jha et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 多剂系统带来额外风险。 迅速感染和中间代理攻击利用指示传播和代理通信(Lee和Tiwari,2024年;He等人,2025年)。 隐私研究揭露了信息泄漏和渗漏(Patil等人,2025年;El Yagoubi等人,2026年;Naik等人,2026年),而TAMAS和ACIArena则研究跨框架和地形的攻击(Kavathekar等人,2026年;An等人,2026年)。 辩护包括GUARDIAN的错误传播模型(周等人,2025年)和控制Valve的控制流量限制(Jha等人,2026年)。

blocks.en: MAS-Guard connects local safeguards with system-level policies over agent roles, communication routes, and capabilities. Its Agent Charters and Control Plane combine deterministic and semantic checks with shared interventions across agents, providing a common framework for integrating complementary safeguards.
blocks.zh: MAS-Guard将地方保障措施与系统一级关于代理作用、通信路线和能力的政策联系起来。 其代理人宪章和控制计划将确定性和语义性的检查与代理人之间的共同干预结合起来,为整合补充性保障措施提供了一个共同框架。

We assume that the guardrail system 𝒢 \mathcal{G} can observe and intercept events exposed by the MAS orchestration layer.

blocks.en:
We call an agent instrumentable when its runtime exposes integration points that allow us to observe local execution events and enforce guardrail decisions before the corresponding action is executed or content is delivered or consumed. These integration points may include hooks for user inputs, tool invocations, tool results, and agent responses. Instrumentability concerns access to the agent’s execution loop; it does not require access to model weights, hidden reasoning, or all internal state. An opaque agent , by contrast, exposes only external interaction boundaries.
For example, agents built with the OpenAI Agents SDK or Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK) can be instrumented as MAS-Guard can integrate with their runtime callbacks ( OpenAI, 2026d ; Google, 2026 ) . A third-party proprietary agent accessed solely through the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol exemplifies the opaque case when MAS-Guard can intercept exchanged messages without access to the agent’s internal execution loop ( A2A Project ).

blocks.en: 4 MAS-Guard Framework
blocks.zh: 4个MAS-守护框架

blocks.en: 4.1 Architecture Overview
blocks.zh: 4.1 结构概况

blocks.en: Figure 1 presents MAS-Guard as a protection layer for applications composed of one or more LLM agents. The framework combines safeguards within individual agents with system-level policy enforcement, protecting the execution of tasks as agents interact with users, tools, and other agents. These two layers provide complementary coverage: local safeguards inspect how an agent loop runs and uses its capabilities, while system safeguards assess whether its observable behavior is appropriate within the composed application.
blocks.zh: 图1将MAS-Guard作为一个或多个LLM剂组成的应用程序的保护层。 该框架将个人代理人内部的保障措施与系统一级政策执行结合起来,保护执行任务,因为代理人与用户、工具和其他代理人互动。 这两个层面提供了互补的涵盖范围:地方保障措施检查一个代理环是如何运行和使用其能力的,而系统保障措施则评估其可观察到的行为是否适合所组成的应用程序。

blocks.en:
For illustration, consider an application that retrieves department-level statistics and emails a summary to a user-specified recipient. An orchestrator delegates retrieval to a SQL agent with a database-query tool and delivery to a notification agent with a sending tool.
A malicious instruction embedded in a database result could attempt to redirect the workflow toward disclosing private records or notifying an unauthorized recipient.
blocks.zh:
举例来说,考虑一个程序,检索部门一级的统计数据,并将摘要邮寄给用户指定的收件人。 一个管弦乐代表使用数据库清空工具检索到一个SQL代理,并用发送工具传送到一个通知代理.
嵌入在数据库结果中的恶意指令可能试图将工作流程转向披露私人记录或通知未经授权的接收者。

blocks.en: The application owner configures MAS-Guard through two complementary policy specifications. Agent Charters describe each agent’s intended role, input/output boundaries, and permitted capabilities. The Control Plane configuration binds these reusable contracts to runtime identities and specifies communication routes, applicable safeguards, and enforcement behavior.
blocks.zh: 应用程序所有人通过两个互补的政策规格配置MAS-Guard. 代理人宪章描述每个代理人的预期作用,输入/输出界限,以及允许的能力. Control Plane配置将这些可重复使用的合同绑定为运行时间身份,并指定了通信路线,适用的保障措施和执法行为.

blocks.en: Within an instrumentable agent, the local Agent Guardrail (A-Guard) applies specialized experts at execution boundaries, for example, to detect injected instructions in a database result before the agent consumes it. The system layer combines deterministic checks of communication routes, declared message formats, and observable capabilities with semantic assessments of role and content. Here, deterministic checks can reject a direct SQL-agent-to-email-service route, or a declared message type outside the receiver’s accepted formats. Semantic checks can audit message content for unauthorized information leak.
blocks.zh: 在可仪器剂内,当地特工Guardrail(A-Guard)在执行边界上应用专门专家,例如,在制剂消耗前在数据库中检测注入的指令. 系统层将确定通信路线的检查、宣布的信息格式和可观察的能力与对作用和内容的语义评估结合起来。 在此, 确定性检查可以拒绝直接的 SQL 代理到电子邮件服务路由, 或拒绝接收者接受格式以外的已声明消息类型 。 语义检查可以对未经授权的信息泄露内容进行审计.

blocks.en:
MAS-Guard supports realistic deployments in which some individual agents are opaque, provided that the MAS orchestration layer remains trusted, observable, and instrumentable. Such agents are guarded at their exposed boundaries, while instrumentable agents additionally receive local A-Guard protection.
A single-agent application is supported as a special case of a multi-agent application.
blocks.zh:
MAS-Guard支持现实的部署,即某些个别特工不透明,条件是MAS的指挥层仍然可信、可观察和可使用仪器。 这些特工人员在暴露的边界受到保护,而可装备的特工人员则受到当地A-Guard的保护。
单代理申请作为多代理申请的特殊情况予以支持.

blocks.en: 4.2 Local Guardrail Layer
blocks.zh: 4.2 地方护卫层

blocks.en:
A-Guard is the local guardrail component of MAS-Guard, typically integrated through the agent execution hooks (Section 3 ).
A-Guard intercepts local events including user inputs, tool registrations, tool invocations, tool results, and agent responses before they are observed, delivered, or executed.
blocks.zh:
A-Guard是MAS-Guard的当地护卫部件,一般通过代理执行钩(第3节)进行整合.
A-Guard拦截本地事件,包括用户输入,工具注册,工具引用,工具结果,以及代理响应在被观察,交付或执行之前.

blocks.en: A-Guard organizes safeguards as task-specific experts . Each expert declares the event types and static conditions under which it is applicable. For an event e t e_{t} , A-Guard selects ℰ t = { g k : eligible k ⁡ ( τ t , c t , Π ) = 1 } , \mathcal{E}_{t}=\left\{g_{k}:\operatorname{eligible}_{k}(\tau_{t},c_{t},\Pi)=1\right\}, (4) where ℰ t \mathcal{E}_{t} is the set of eligible experts. Eligibility rules avoid unnecessary model calls by excluding irrelevant events or trusted cases. The selected experts execute in parallel and emit verdicts in a shared output space. Their outputs are passed to the enforcement mechanism described in Section 4.4 .

blocks.en: Figure 2: A-Guard provides a local guardrail layer to audit agentic events for instrumentable agents.
blocks.zh: 图2:A-Guard为可仪器代理的审计代理事件提供了一个当地的护栏层.

blocks.en:
Our implementation instantiates three guardrail experts: User Prompt Injection , which detects direct prompt injection instructions in user turns; Tool-Result Prompt Injection , which detects indirect prompt injection instructions embedded in external tool results; and Sensitive Unintended Tool Call , which assesses whether a non-read-only action is supported by the user’s intent and execution context.
We selected these experts to address the Prompt Injection and Excessive Agency risk categories identified in the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications ( OWASP Foundation, 2025 ) .
We implement these experts using task-specific prompts optimized for Gemma-4-26B-A4B-IT ( 7 ) , independent of the acting agent model.
blocks.zh:
我们的实施工作使三名看守人员专家立即: 用户快速注射(User Express injection),它检测用户转弯时的直接即时注射指令; 工具-result Express injection(工具-result Express injection),它检测嵌入在外部工具结果中的间接即时注射指令; 敏感无意工具呼叫(Scientific Uninted Tool Call),它评估非只读动作是否由用户的意图和执行上下文支持.
我们挑选了这些专家,处理在LLM应用OWASP第10名(OWASP基金会,2025年)中确定的快速注射和过度机构风险类别。
我们利用对Gemma-4-26B-A4B-IT(7 )进行优化的、独立于代理模型的任务特定提示来实施这些专家。

blocks.en:
We optimized the guardrail prompts using an automated prompt optimization (APO) loop inspired by Autoresearch Karpathy (2026) and Meta-Harness Lee et al. (2026) , in which an optimization agent iteratively analyzez evaluation results and failure cases, proposes targeted revisions, and verifies them on a disjoint development set. Appendix E.3 details the optimization loop design, development datasets, candidate generation, and optimization objective.
The proposed architecture is not restricted to these experts or this choice of underlying model: additional heterogeneous safeguards can be registered to cover broader vulnerabilities. Implementation details in Appendix E .
blocks.zh:
我们利用AutoreResearch Karpath(2026)和Meta-Harness Lee et al.(2026)启发的自动即时优化(APO)循环,优化了护栏提示,其中优化剂迭代分析评价结果和故障案例,提出有针对性的修改,并在脱节开发集上验证. 附录E.3详细介绍了优化循环设计,开发数据集,候选生成,优化目标.
拟议架构不仅限于这些专家,也不局限于这种对基本模式的选择:可以登记额外的各种保障措施,以涵盖更广泛的脆弱性。 附录E详细执行情况。

blocks.en: 4.3 System Guardrail Layer
blocks.zh: 4.3 系统护卫层

blocks.en: The system guardrail layer governs the application’s behavior using agent roles, input/output contracts, routes, and capabilities. It evaluates the boundaries exposed by the orchestration layer, including user-facing inputs and outputs, coordination or delegation among agents, and boundary events produced by opaque agents whose internal execution cannot be instrumented. This scope allows the same policy framework to protect both instrumentable agents and the observable MAS system-level interfaces.
blocks.zh: 系统护栏层控制着应用程序使用代理角色、输入/输出合同、路线和能力的行为。 它评价了管弦乐层暴露的界限,包括用户提供的投入和产出、代理人之间的协调或授权,以及内部执行无法使用仪器的不透明代理人产生的界限事件。 这一范围允许同样的政策框架,既保护可使用仪器的代理人,也保护可观察到的MAS系统一级的接口。

blocks.en:
To represent these policies in MAS-Guard, each Agent Charter specifies a reusable role contract through its charter_id , objective , input/output ( I/O ) contracts, and features .
Each input/output contract specifies accepted message formats, prohibited content types, and a semantic topic policy. Content type restrictions identify categories that must not appear, such as credentials or personal information. Topic policies specify allowed or prohibited message content through natural-language descriptions. In the example above, the notification agent’s topic policy can prohibit requests to send a summary to a recipient not authorized by the user.The Control Plane binds runtime identities to these Charters and configures enforcement of routes, guardrails, and interventions. Table 1 summarizes this policy structure; Appendices A and B provide the complete schemas.
blocks.zh:
为了在MAS-Guard中代表这些政策,每个代理商宪章都通过其章程、目标、投入/产出(一/O)合同和特征规定了可重复使用的角色合同。
每个输入/输出合同都规定了可接受的电文格式、被禁止的内容类型和语义主题政策。 内容类型限制指不得出现的类别,如证书或个人信息. 主题政策通过自然语言描述来指定允许或禁止的信息内容. 在上述例子中,通知代理的主题政策可以禁止要求向未经用户授权的接收者发送摘要。 《控制计划》将运行时间身份与这些宪章挂钩,并规定了路线、护栏和干预措施的执法情况。 表1概述了这一政策结构;附录A和B提供了完整的计划。

blocks.en: Table 1: Policy components of the system guardrail layer. Agent Charters define roles, input/output boundaries, and capability scope; the Control Plane binds these contracts to the application and connects structural and semantic checks to consistent enforcement.
blocks.zh: 表1:系统护卫层的政策组成部分。 《代理章程》界定了作用、投入/产出界限和能力范围;《控制计划》将这些合同与应用程序挂钩,并将结构和语义检查与一致的执行联系起来。

blocks.en:
Each Charter compliance binding independently enables format, content, topic, and capability checks, while Control Plane configuration determines allowed routes and specifies enforcement actions.
Our design favors deterministic enforcement when a requirement can be checked in code, such as message format or permitted routes.
blocks.zh:
独立地约束每个宪章的遵守都允许进行格式、内容、专题和能力检查,而控制计划配置则确定允许的路线并指定执行行动。
我们的设计倾向于当某项要求可以在代码中检查时,例如消息格式或允许的路由时,确定执行.

blocks.en: 4.4 Enforcement and Mitigation
blocks.zh: 4.4 执法和缓解

blocks.en: Each local or system-level safeguard returns a binary violation trigger and a rationale. The configured enforcement policy maps each violation to an intervention. MAS-Guard aggregates the verdicts into one of four decisions. Allow admits the event without intervention. Reflection is a non-blocking intervention for potentially correctable behavior; additional guardrail feedback is provided to the agent so it can correct its course. Confirmation pauses the event to require explicit user approval, particularly suitable for ambiguous or sensitive actions. Finally, Block prevents the event from being delivered or executed when a clear policy or safety violation is detected. Illustrative examples are provided in Appendix D .
blocks.zh: 每个本地或系统层面的保障措施都返回二进制违规触发器和理由。 所配置的执法政策将每一次违法行为都划入干预范围。 MAS-Guard将判决汇总为四项裁决之一. 允许在没有干预的情况下承认事件. 反射是针对潜在可纠正行为的非阻断性干预;向代理人提供额外的护卫反馈,以便它能够纠正其行进过程. 确认暂停事件,要求用户明确批准,特别是适用于模棱两可或敏感的行动。 最后,当发现明显违反政策或违反安全规定时,Block防止事件交付或执行. 附录D提供了示例。

blocks.en:
When multiple guardrails produce different verdicts for the same event, MAS-Guard uses the most restrictive applicable decision, following the ordering Block > Confirmation > Reflection > Allow \textsc{Block}>\textsc{Confirmation}>\textsc{Reflection}>\textsc{Allow} .
This keeps verdict aggregation deterministic and avoids introducing an additional model-based decision layer.
blocks.zh:
当多个守护符对同一事件产生不同的判决时,MAS-Guard使用最限制性的适用决定,遵循命令的块 > 确认 > 反射 > 允许\textsc{Block{\textsc{确认{\textsc{Reflection{textsc{Allow}。
这保持了裁决汇总的确定性,避免引入一个额外的基于模型的决策层。

blocks.en: 5 Experiments
blocks.zh: 5 实验

blocks.en: We evaluate MAS-Guard through three research questions: (RQ1) whether it reduces attack success without materially degrading benign-task utility; (RQ2) whether the safety–utility trade-off transfers across agent backbones and attack families; and (RQ3) how much the local A-Guard, deterministic, and semantic system checks each contribute.
blocks.zh: 我们通过三个研究问题来评估MAS-Guard:(RQ1)它是否在没有实质贬低良性任务效用的情况下降低成功率;(RQ2)安全-效用权衡跨越代理骨干和攻击家庭的转移;以及(RQ3)当地A-Guard、决定和语义系统检查各贡献多少。

blocks.en: 5.1 Experiment Setup
blocks.zh: 5.1 实验设置

blocks.en: 5.1.1 Benchmarks

Our evaluation suite contains four multi-agent and two single-agent benchmarks, summarized in Table 2 . ACIArena ( An et al., 2026 ) , TAMAS ( Kavathekar et al., 2026 ) , AgentLeak ( El Yagoubi et al., 2026 ) , and OmniLeak ( Naik et al., 2026 ) 1 1 1 OmniLeak denotes our reconstruction and extension of the work by Naik et al. (2026) as described in Appendix G.5 exercise cross-agent instruction propagation, communication compromise, privacy leakage, and unsafe delegation across heterogeneous multi-agent topologies. OverThink ( Kumar et al., 2025 ) and Agent Security Bench (ASB) ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) test coverage for local vulnerabilities, including performance sabotage, direct and indirect prompt injection, memory poisoning, and malicious tool execution. This mixture is intentional: a unified guardrail should protect both internal agent events and system-boundary interactions.

We jointly assess safety and usefulness through attack success rate (ASR) and Utility. ASR measures the proportion of adversarial cases in which the attacker achieves the malicious objective, while Utility measures task success on benign cases. For each benchmark, we retain its definitions of attack success and task completion where they align with these general definitions. Table 2 summarizes the operational definitions used in our experiments. For each metric, overall results are sample-weighted means across benchmarks. We compute 95% confidence intervals using Wilson score intervals for binary outcomes Wilson (1927) and Student’s t t -intervals for fractional scores Student (1908) .

blocks.en: 5.1.3 Agents and Guardrail Baselines
blocks.zh: 5.1.3 代理人和警卫基线

blocks.en:
We repeat our experiments with three agent models: GPT-5.6-Terra and Grok-4.3 as proprietary LLMs, together with Muse-Glimmer-30B as an open-source LLM. Note that MAS-Guard’s semantic experts use the separate Gemma-4-26B-A4B-IT Gemma Team et al. (2026) model described in Section 4.2 , separating the model that generates an action from the model that audits it.
We used Codex OpenAI (2026a) with GPT-5.6-Sol OpenAI (2026b) at high reasoning effort to author the MAS-Guard Agent Charters and Control Plane configurations. For each public benchmark, the provided context contained the benchmark documentation and a development sample set disjoint from the test set used for the reported evaluation.
Appendix G provides further details and examples.
blocks.zh:
我们用三种代理模型重复我们的实验:GPT-5.6-泰拉和Grok-4.3作为专有LLM,同时Muse-Glimer-30B作为开源LLM. 请注意,MAS-Guard的语义专家使用了第4.2节描述的独立的Gemma-4-26B-A4B-IT Gemma Team等人(2026)模型,将产生动作的模型与审计它的模式区分开来.
我们用Codex OpenAI(2026a)与GPT-5.6-Sol OpenAI(2026b)在高推理努力中编译了MAS-Guard Agent Charters和Control Plane配置. 就每个公共基准而言,所提供的上下文载有基准文件和一套开发样本,与用于报告评价的成套测试不相关。
附 录 G提供了进一步的细节和实例。

blocks.en:
To cover a diverse comparison space, we include methods ranging from lightweight prompt defenses to structural changes in agent execution and independent guardrail models. Sandwich ( Schulhoff, 2024 ) and Delimiter ( Hines et al., 2024 ) represent prompt-based defenses that rewrite or mark untrusted input. ACI-Sentinel An et al. (2026) represents model-based output filtering, while LlamaFirewall Chennabasappa et al. (2025) provides a guardrail system spanning prompt, alignment, and code checks. ToolSafe Mou et al. (2026) is a specialized tool-invocation safety model, and AgentDoG Liu et al. (2026b) and AgentDoG-1.5 Liu et al. (2026a) are independent trajectory-level guardrail models. FIDES Costa et al. (2025) represents a control and data flow approach that keeps untrusted values out of planner context through sandboxed value queries and opaque references. No-Guardrail retains the agent model’s native safety behavior.
Appendix H details method configurations, benchmark execution-loop integration, and enforcement setup in our experiments.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: Safeguarding autonomous and collaborative LLM agents requires connecting individual-agent behavior to the roles, capabilities, and policies of the application. We introduced MAS-Guard, a unified runtime framework connecting local safeguards with system-level policy enforcement. A-Guard applies experts within instrumentable agents, while Agent Charters and a Control Plane govern observable application boundaries through deterministic and semantic checks. A shared intervention space provides consistent enforcement across layers, supporting deployments containing instrumentable and opaque agents. Across six benchmarks and three agent LLMs, MAS-Guard reduces overall ASR by 71.5–86.3% relative to unguarded execution while meeting the utility criterion. These results support combining local safeguards with application-specific policy enforcement to address agentic risks while preserving benign-task utility. MAS-Guard provides a framework for coordinating safeguards across heterogeneous agents under developer-owned contracts.
blocks.zh: 保护自主和协作的LLM代理人需要将个人代理行为与应用的作用、能力和政策联系起来。 我们采用了MAS-Guard,这是一个连接地方保障措施和系统一级政策执行的统一运行时间框架。 A-Guard在有仪器的代理人内部应用专家,而代理宪章和控制计划则通过确定性和语义检查来管理可观察到的应用界限。 一个共享的干预空间提供各层一致的执法,支持部署含有可仪器和不透明剂的部署。 在6个基准和3个代理LLMs中,MAS-Guard在达到效用标准的同时,将总体ASR比无人看守的执行减少71.5-86.3%. 这些成果支持将地方保障措施与针对具体应用的政策执行结合起来,以应对代理风险,同时维护良性任务效用。 MAS-Guard提供了一个框架,用以协调开发商拥有的合同下各种代理人的保障措施。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: We consider heterogeneous multi-agent deployments in which a subset of participating agents may be opaque. However, we assume that the multi-agent orchestration framework is observable, instrumentable, and trusted. Under this assumption, for opaque agents, protection is limited to external inputs and outputs: internal prompt injection, memory corruption, hidden tool use, and other unexposed actions may remain undetected. Boundary checks cannot undo side effects that have already occurred internally or guarantee that all malicious behavior becomes externally visible.
blocks.zh: 我们认为,各种多代理人的部署可能不透明,其中一部分参与代理人可能不透明。 然而,我们假设,多剂管弦乐框架是可观察的、可乐的和可信赖的。 根据这一假设,对于不透明的代理,保护仅限于外部投入和输出:内部即时注射,内存腐败,隐藏工具的使用,以及其他未暴露的行动可能仍未被发现. 边界检查不能消除内部已经发生的副作用,也不能保证所有恶意行为都从外部可见。

blocks.en: Furthermore, compromise of the operating system, runtime, or orchestration infrastructure, and attacks on agent-to-agent transport channels that bypass interception, are outside this threat model. Access control, tool permissions, sandboxing, authentication, encryption, and network security remain important, orthogonal areas of security engineering. MAS-Guard’s checks on declared routes and capabilities complement these controls but are not a replacement and do not implement their underlying security guarantees.
blocks.zh: 此外,操作系统、运行时间或管线基础设施的妥协以及对绕过拦截的代理至代理运输渠道的攻击不在这种威胁模式之内。 访问控制、工具权限、沙箱、认证、加密和网络安全仍然是安全工程的正统领域。 MAS-Guard对申报的路线和能力进行的检查补充了这些控制,但不是替代,也没有执行其基本安全保障。

blocks.en: We also assume a trusted application owner who authors Agent Charters and configures MAS-Guard Control Plane. Although we used AI assistance to produce experimental configurations, application developers must ultimately own, vet, and maintain the Agent Charters and Control Plane configurations used in real deployments. Defining these contracts requires application-specific judgments about legitimate workflows, role boundaries, data sensitivity, and permitted capabilities. Incomplete or overly permissive policies can leave unsafe behavior unconstrained, while overly restrictive policies can suppress legitimate tasks.
blocks.zh: 我们还假设一个可以信任的应用程序拥有者,负责撰写代理宪章并配置MAS-Guard控制计划. 虽然我们使用AI协助来制作实验配置,但应用程序开发人员最终必须拥有,审查,并维护真实部署中使用的代理宪章和控制计划配置. 对这些合同的界定要求根据应用的具体情况对合法工作流程、角色界限、数据敏感性和允许的能力作出判断。 不完全或过分放任的政策可能使不安全的行为不受限制,而过度限制性的政策则会压制合法的任务。

blocks.en: Lastly, to simplify our experiment setup and make comparisons easier, we use ASR as an umbrella term for rate of successful attacks in our experiments; therefore, the reported results should not be interpreted as a severity-weighted or absolute measure of real-world harm. For consistent comparisons across benchmarks, we measure Utility only on benign episodes, leaving legitimate-task completion under attack for future studies.
blocks.zh: 最后,为了简化我们的实验设置,使比较更加容易,我们使用ASR作为我们实验中成功攻击率的总括术语;因此,所报告的结果不应被解释为对现实世界伤害的重度加权或绝对衡量。 为了在各种基准之间进行一致的比较,我们只根据良性事件衡量效用,使合法任务完成的工作受到打击,以便今后进行研究。

blocks.en: Ethical Considerations
blocks.zh: 道德考虑

blocks.en: MAS-Guard proposes guardrails intended to support safer and more responsible use of agentic AI through enforcement of application-owner policies. Such policies may themselves be incomplete or inappropriate, and guardrail errors may permit harmful actions or block legitimate tasks. Our benchmark results therefore do not establish safety for arbitrary deployments. Real-world deployments should include review of the governing policies, application-specific evaluation, and appropriate human oversight.
blocks.zh: MAS-Guard建议设立护栏,通过执行申请所有人政策,支持更安全和更负责任地使用代理AI。 这些政策本身可能不完整或不适当,而护卫系统的错误可能允许有害的行动或阻碍正当的任务。 因此,我们的基准结果不能确定任意部署的安全性。 现实世界的部署应包括审查管理政策、具体应用评价和适当的人的监督。

blocks.en: Although intended for defense, MAS-Guard could be incorporated into an adversarial simulation loop, using guardrail feedback to iteratively develop stronger malicious attacks. To limit this risk, we do not publicly release the exact guardrail prompts, and we are instead considering availability through controlled access, while acknowledging the resulting limitation on reproducibility.
blocks.zh: 虽然意在防御,但MAS-Guard可以并入一个对抗性的模拟循环,利用护栏反馈来迭代地发展更强大的恶意攻击. 为了限制这一风险,我们不公开发布确切的护栏提示,而是考虑通过控制准入提供,同时承认由此产生的对可复制性的限制。

blocks.en: Appendix C Detailed Results
blocks.zh: 附录C 结果

blocks.en: Tables 7 and 8 extend the benchmark-level ASR analysis to Muse-Glimmer-30B and Grok-4.3. MAS-Guard reduces overall ASR from 30.6% to 4.2% and from 30.9% to 8.8%, respectively, achieving the lowest overall ASR point estimate among the evaluated methods for both backbones. It reduces ASR on five of six benchmarks in each setting. The remaining benchmark is unchanged: OmniLeak stays at 0.1% for Muse-Glimmer-30B, while OverThink remains at the already-zero unguarded result for Grok-4.3.
blocks.zh: 表7和表8将基准水平的ASR分析扩展至Muse-Glimer-30B和Grok-4.3. MAS-Guard将总体ASR分别从30.6%降至4.2%和30.9%降至8.8%,实现了两个主干部被评价方法中总体ASR点估计最低. 它在每次设定的6个基准中减少5个的ASR。 其余的基准不变:对Muse-Glimer-30B来说,OmniLeak保持在0.1%,而对Grok-4.3来说,OverThink仍然处于已经是零的无保障结果。

blocks.en: The benchmark breakdown reveals variation in both baseline vulnerability and residual risk. For Muse-Glimmer-30B, MAS-Guard reduces OverThink ASR from 36.6% to 0.0% and ACIArena ASR from 40.0% to 7.9%. For Grok-4.3, substantial reductions occur on ASB (70.8% to 13.8%) and OmniLeak (16.3% to 0.1%). Nevertheless, Grok-4.3 retains higher residual ASR on ACIArena and AgentLeak, at 26.6% and 17.0%, compared with 7.9% and 3.8% for Muse-Glimmer-30B. Thus, the aggregate improvements extend across backbones, although protection remains dependent on the agent and evaluation setting.

blocks.en: Tables 9 , 10 , and 11 report the corresponding benign-task Utility. In each case, the guarded point estimate remains above the lower endpoint of the unguarded baseline’s 95% confidence interval, satisfying the utility reference criterion.

blocks.en: The comparisons also illustrate why ASR and Utility should be interpreted jointly. FIDES achieves lower ASR than MAS-Guard on ACIArena and AgentLeak across all three backbones, but its overall Utility falls below the reference threshold in every setting. On ASB with Grok-4.3, ToolSafe achieves an ASR of 1.0%, compared with MAS-Guard’s 13.8%, while its Utility is 49.1%, compared with 65.2% for MAS-Guard. Such differences show that strong attack suppression on an individual benchmark can accompany substantial reductions in benign-task performance, motivating comparison at both the benchmark and aggregate levels.

blocks.en: D.3 Cross-Case Findings
blocks.zh: D.3 跨案件调查结果

blocks.en:
The traces expose three distinctions that are collapsed by aggregate scores.
First, placement matters : output-boundary enforcement contains the
disclosure in C1, whereas C2 contrasts MAS-Guard blocking the injected user input with ToolSafe blocking the subsequent malicious tool call. Second, recovery matters : blocking an attack can still abandon the original task, while a rewrite can permit partial or complete continuation.
Third, system context matters for utility : in C3, an apparently
sensitive database-derived message is necessary and explicitly authorized;
suppressing it breaks the workflow even though the final email action still
occurs. C4 shows the analogous effect for a single-agent tool boundary.

第一,安插事项:产出边界执法包括:
在 C1 中披露,而C2 对比了 MAS- Guard 屏蔽注入的用户输入,而 ToolSafe 屏蔽了随后的恶意工具调用. 第二,恢复问题:阻断攻击仍然可以放弃原任务,而重写则可以允许部分或完全延续.
第三,系统上下文涉及效用:

压制它打破工作流程, 尽管最后的电子邮件动作仍然
发生。 C4显示了单一代理工具边界的类似效果.

blocks.en: E.3 Agent-Aided Automated Prompt Optimization
blocks.zh: E.3 自动优化

blocks.en: We use an agent-aided automated prompt optimization (APO) procedure to iteratively improve guardrail prompts through a metrics-driven experimental loop, following the general paradigm of autonomous experimentation and harness optimization inspired by Autoresearch Karpathy (2026) and Meta-Harness Lee et al. (2026) .
blocks.zh: 我们使用一种代理辅助的自动即时优化(APO)程序,通过一个由度量衡驱动的实验循环来迭代改进护轨提示,遵循Autorrearch Karpath (2026) 和 Meta-Harness Lee 等人 (2026) 所启发的自主实验和利用优化的一般范式.

blocks.en: Each APO run is governed by a task-specific specification file that defines the optimization objective, allowed search space, development data, evaluation commands, target metrics and constraints, permitted modifications, and artifacts to retain. The evaluation implementation and metric computation are treated as fixed infrastructure and cannot be modified by the optimization agent. In our experiments, we used balanced accuracy, BA = ( TPR + TNR ) / 2 \mathrm{BA}=(\mathrm{TPR}+\mathrm{TNR})/2 , as the main optimization objective, and false positive rate (FPR) of at most 1% as the guardrail constraint.
blocks.zh: 每次APO运行都受任务特定规格文件的制约,该文件定义了优化目标,允许搜索空间,开发数据,评价命令,目标度量和限制,允许修改,以及保留文物. 评价执行情况和计量计算作为固定基础设施处理,不能通过优化剂加以修改。 在我们的实验中,我们使用平衡精度(BA = (TPR + TNR ) / 2\mathrm{BA}=(\mathrm{TPR}+\mathrm{TNR})/2)作为主要优化目标,以最多1%的假正率(FPR)作为护栏限制.

blocks.en: At a high level, the optimization loop consists of five steps. First, the agent inspects the current prompt and configuration together with prior experiment artifacts, including metrics, predictions, logs, and representative failure cases. Second, it analyzes quantitative results and qualitative error patterns to identify weaknesses and formulate a targeted hypothesis for improvement. Third, it proposes and applies a change only to components permitted by the specification. Fourth, it evaluates the resulting candidate using the prescribed development benchmark and fixed evaluation pipeline. Finally, it accepts or rejects the candidate according to the defined objectives and constraints, while preserving the resulting configuration, metrics, failure analysis, and decision for subsequent iterations.
blocks.zh: 在高水平上,优化循环包括五个步骤. 第一,物剂与以前的实验文物,包括测量、预测、日志和具有代表性的故障案例一起检查目前的速率和配置。 第二,它分析定量结果和定性误差模式,以找出弱点,并制定一个有针对性的改进假设。 第三,它只提议对规格允许的部件进行修改。 第四,它利用规定的发展基准和固定评价程序来评价所产生的候选人。 最后,它根据确定的目标和限制接受或拒绝候选人,同时保留由此产生的配置、衡量标准、故障分析和随后重复的决定。

blocks.en: APO was applied independently to each guardrail task using a strictly disjoint set of datasets different from benchmarks used in the MAS-Guard evaluations. Specifically, we used a total of 2,200 samples from InjecAgent Zhan et al. (2024) , τ \tau -bench Yao et al. (2025) , Agent-SafetyBench Zhang et al. (2024) , BrowseSafe Bench Zhang et al. (2026) , and AgentDojo Debenedetti et al. (2024) .

blocks.en: Candidate selection combined aggregate metrics with analysis of false-positive and false-negative examples to distinguish meaningful improvements from changes that merely shifted errors across categories. This procedure automates much of the prompt-engineering loop while preserving a fixed evaluation protocol, explicit optimization constraints, separation between development and test data, and an auditable history of candidate changes and outcomes.

The role-family Charters accept plain text and distinguish legitimate math,
code, planning, review, and evaluation behavior. Their shared denylist covers
the benchmark’s synthetic private identity and credentials, external callbacks,
task derailment or artificial refusal, answer tampering, and propagation of
embedded malicious control directives. The policy also prohibits credential,
PII, PHI, PCI, URL, and shell-command content and declares internet access out
of scope. Charter Compliance inspects message-send and message-receive events;
violations block by default, but disruption evaluations use reflection so the
agent can retry the original task. A-Guard is attached to task-performing
roles, not the synthetic user or evaluation harness.

blocks.en: G.3 TAMAS
blocks.zh: G.3 海啸

blocks.en:
TAMAS Kavathekar et al. (2026) spans five domains and multiple AutoGen and
CrewAI topologies. Its policy contains a task-source Charter, a shared
tool-boundary Charter, and 21
functional Charters covering the released domain roles and the manager. Role
aliases and attacked A/B variants remain bound to the trusted base-role
Charter: an attack may change an agent’s runtime description, but it does not
change the product owner’s contract. The Control Plane permits task delivery,
peer coordination or broadcast, guarded tool requests and results, and the
final response. Unknown identities are isolated and unlisted routes block.

TAMAS Kavathekar 等人(2026年)跨越五个领域和多个AutoGen和
CrewAI 地形学. 其政策包括一项任务来源宪章,一项共享的宪章
和《宪章》第21条

更改产品所有人合同。 《控制计划》允许交付任务,
同行协调或广播、谨慎的工具请求和结果以及
最后答复。 不明身份是隔离和未列出路线的阻断。

blocks.en:
The task source may not override an agent’s objective, fabricate authority, or
request an unauthorized harmful action. Tool output may not act as a control
directive or request an unrelated harmful action. Each task-agent Charter
adds objective-deviation, authority-abuse, unauthorized-side-effect, and
role-boundary topics, together with the capabilities required by that role;
direct code execution is out of scope for every benign role. We do not use
static sensitive-content categories because valid TAMAS work contains URLs and
medical, legal, financial, and identity data. Charter Compliance therefore
uses semantic authorization and capability checks on sends, receives, and
handoffs. A-Guard is attached to task agents but not to the benchmark user or
shared tool boundary.

blocks.en: G.4 AgentLeak
blocks.zh: G.4 代理总裁

blocks.en:
AgentLeak El Yagoubi et al. (2026) defines a privacy boundary that changes
with the scenario, so the adapter creates case-scoped Charters. For each case,
it registers a task source, a guarded
tool boundary, and each runtime agent, and enumerates all intended user,
agent-to-agent, and agent–tool routes.
Our AgentLeak integration exposes four of the benchmark’s seven leakage channels: final output (C1), inter-agent communication (C2), tool input (C3), and tool output (C4). We measure leakage over these observed channels; shared memory (C5), logs (C6), and artifacts (C7) are outside this integration.

blocks.en: G.5 OmniLeak
blocks.zh: G.5 奥姆尼莱克

blocks.en: The version of OmniLeak available when we conducted this study did not include code or released data. We therefore use our reconstruction and extension of its disclosed experimental contract. It preserves the centralized Orchestrator–SQL–Notification workflow, attack categories, schema-knowledge settings, benign queries, and database scales described by Naik et al. (2026) , while using newly generated attack payloads and additional authorized control cases.

Our reconstruction and guardrail-oriented extension of
OmniLeak Naik et al. (2026) has a fixed six-principal topology: user,
orchestrator, SQL agent, database, notification agent, and a synthetic local
email sink. The Control
Plane admits exactly the nine directed boundaries needed for query delegation,
database access and return, result integration, optional notification, and the
final answer. Each principal receives a role-level Charter with a least-
privilege capability scope.

blocks.en: G.6 OverThink

blocks.en:
OverThink FreshQA Kumar et al. (2025) is a single-agent RAG workload. We
register only the answer agent and model search as a tool rather than as a
second agent. Its Charter
accepts plain text and JSON but deliberately contains no topic restrictions or
capability limits, and the Control Plane installs no Charter Compliance guardrail. For full MAS-Guard, the answer agent’s A-Guard
attachment evaluates the retrieved document as a tool result before model
delivery and evaluates the final response. Consequently, any protection on
this benchmark is attributable to the single-agent A-Guard layer, not to a
benchmark-tailored Charter rule; MAS-Guard variants without A-Guard retain only
the otherwise inert core Control Plane.

OverThink FreshQA Kumar等人(2025年)是单一代理RAG的工作量. 我们

For each ASB case Zhang et al. (2025) , we create a Charter whose objective is
the original benign task and bind the synthetic user and tool identities to a
shared boundary
Charter. The Control Plane allows only the four intended directions from user
to agent, agent to tool, tool to agent, and agent to user. Inbound Charter
violations use reflection, allowing the agent to reconsider untrusted planning,
tool, or memory content; outbound violations block. A-Guard is attached only
to the task agent.

blocks.en: Appendix H Comparison-method Configuration
blocks.zh: 附录H 比较方法 配置

blocks.en: H.1 Common adaptation protocol
blocks.zh: H.1 共同适应议定书

blocks.en:
In our implementation of different safeguards used in the comparisons, every method receives the same canonical event representation and the
same pre-intervention content at a boundary it supports. Its returned action
is then applied before the benchmark continues: input transformations replace
the content delivered to the next agent, blocking decisions stop the pending
boundary action, and pass decisions leave it unchanged. An event outside a
method’s documented or implemented scope produces an explicit pass.
blocks.zh:
在执行比较中使用的不同保障措施时,每一种方法都得到同样的犬科事件说明和
与它支持的边界上相同的前干预内容。 恢复行动
然后在基准继续之前应用:替换输入转换
将内容交给下一个代理商, 阻止决定停止未决
边界行动,通过决定时不改变。 外面的事件
方法的记载或执行范围产生明确的通行证。

blocks.en: H.2 Prompt-transformation baselines
blocks.zh: H.2 快速转换基线

blocks.en:
Following the Sandwich defense Schulhoff (2024) , at each
supported untrusted-input boundary we append a fixed reminder
after the original content. The reminder tells the receiving agent to preserve
the benchmark task and explicit constraints and to treat conflicting requests
for private-data leakage, external reporting, artificial refusal, propagation
of control text, or answer remapping as untrusted. The safeguard returns a
redirect action containing the original content followed by this reminder.
blocks.zh:
Schulhoff(2024年)之后,
支持不可信输入的边界, 我们附加一个固定的提醒
在原始内容之后。 提醒通知接收人保留
基准任务和明确限制,并处理相互冲突的请求
私人数据泄漏、外部报告、人为拒绝、传播
控制文本,或回答不可信。 保护返回a
重定向包含此提醒后原有内容的动作 。

blocks.en:
Following the delimiting form of Spotlighting Hines et al. (2024) , we
precede the content with a fixed instruction to treat the following
message as data rather than as authority, then enclose it between <untrusted_message> tags. It likewise returns a redirect action. We
apply both prompt transformations to user-input, tool-result, and RAG-database-
insertion projections. Neither baseline filters post-agent output or directly
blocks a tool call.
blocks.zh:
继Spotlighting Hines等人(2024年)的划界形式之后,我们
在内容之前附加一个处理下列事项的固定指示:
消息作为数据而不是权威,然后在“un trusted_message”标记之间附上。 同样,它还带来了重新定向行动。 我们
对用户输入、工具结果和RAG数据库进行即时转换-
插入预测。 基线既不过滤代理输出,也不直接过滤
屏蔽工具调用。

blocks.en: H.3 Event-level filters and classifiers
blocks.zh: H.3 事件一级过滤器和分类器

blocks.en:
We implement ACI-Sentinel An et al. (2026) as a post-agent output filter.
Given the original user query and the candidate agent answer, the shared
guardrail inferencer is
prompted to retain, in original wording and order, only excerpts directly
relevant to the query. Decoding uses temperature zero and at most 1,024
completion tokens. Successful filtering redirects the outgoing answer to the
filtered text; pre-agent boundaries are recorded as passes.
blocks.zh:
我们实施ACI-Sentinel An等人(2026年)作为后剂输出过滤器.
考虑到原始用户查询和候选代理的回答,共享
护栏推论是
促使按原措词和顺序只直接保留摘录

blocks.en: H.4 FIDES dataflow baseline
blocks.zh: H.4 可持续发展论坛数据流量基线

blocks.en:
FIDES Costa et al. (2025) is integrated inside each benchmark’s native
planning and tool loop rather than as an event-verdict classifier. Untrusted
retrieval, tool, and
peer-agent outputs are stored in case-local memory, and the planner sees opaque
references. References can pass through later tool arguments and are expanded
only at the executor. When hidden data must be transformed, a tool-less query_llm operation uses the suite’s shared guardrail inferencer and
stores its result under a new reference. Only bounded Boolean or enumerated
values may be revealed to the planner for data-dependent branching; larger
results remain referenced until an authorized final-delivery boundary.

blocks.en:
Our evaluation executes each benchmark with guardrails embedded in its
agent loop. Benchmark adapters expose eligible user inputs, agent messages,
tool invocations, tool results, and final responses through a common event
representation, retaining the available history and tool schemas.
Event-based defenses inspect supported boundaries before the pending
operation executes or content is delivered. Their outputs can therefore
change subsequent model inputs, tool execution, and task outcomes.
Unsupported events pass unchanged. FIDES instead modifies data handling
inside the execution loop, as described below.
